capitals.name: Florence
capitals.note: Infobox: Florence (1865-1871); Rome falls on 20 September 1870 and is the capital from 1871.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1861 (Cliopatria's first shape is 1862): the kingdom was proclaimed on 17 March 1861 and the 1862 outline stands for the proclamation year. Infobox area 250,320 km2 (1861) against Cliopatria's 235,522 km2 for 1862: ratio 0.94, fine.

correction.text: the 1868 shape from October 1866 and for 1867 (Veneto, Friuli and Mantua)

keyframe_review.note: 242,248 km2, 1866-1867, with only 24 of Veneto's 71 cells. Use the 1868 shape (Veneto 67 cells, Friuli 25) from October 1866.

261,747 km2, 1868-1870: Italy with Veneto and Friuli but without Rome (Lazio 13 of 63 cells). Right until 20 September 1870 (Kingdom page: 'Italian troops entered Rome in 1870'). Cliopatria dates the Veneto cells two years after the October 1866 treaty.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1885-1889 (years change only)

keyframe_review.note: 277,741 km2, 1885-1904: adds 10 Eritrean cells (Massawa, Assab). Italian Empire page: Assab taken over by the Italian government in 1882, Massawa annexed in 1885, Eritrea a colony from the Treaty of Wuchale of 1889; Cliopatria's Italian Africa row draws the colony from 1890, so these cells are drawn twice in 1890-1904. Valid as drawn for 1885-1889 only; from 1890 use the new 1890 keyframe. The Tientsin concession (1901) is missing from this shape until 1905.

New keyframe, 1890-1904: the 1885 shape without Eritrea, which the Italian Africa dossier (type colony, a tint of the metropole) carries from 1890. The page's Eritrea dates: 1882 (infobox), 1885 (Massawa), 1889 (Wuchale); it gives no 1890.

275,058 km2, 1905-1911: Italy and a 2-cell patch at Tientsin. Kingdom page: 'On 7 September 1901, a concession in Tientsin was ceded to Italy by the Qing Dynasty' and taken into possession on 7 June 1902; the shape adds it four years late.

277,575 km2, 1912-1915: adds the Dodecanese (6 Greek cells). Italian Empire page: the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne 'formalized Italian administration of both Libya and the Dodecanese Islands'; the page is silent on May 1912. Libya is drawn by the Italian Africa and Libya dossiers, not by this shape.
277,720 km2, 1916 only: the 1912 outline. Unchanged within the precision of the sources (unverified: page budget; no page opened covers the First World War front).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but its Albanian cells are a protectorate drawn as a vassal tint (status change only)

keyframe_review.note: 285,113 km2, 1917 only: adds 25 Albanian cells. Italian Empire page: 'In June 1917, general Giacinto Ferrero proclaimed the Italian-controlled territory in Albania to be independent under Italian protection': the Albanian cells are a protectorate (vassal tint), not Italian territory.

272,287 km2, 1918 only: Friuli (0 of 30 cells) and part of Veneto (41 of 71) are missing, which suggests an enemy-held north-east for the year; no page opened covers the First World War front, so the shape is kept (unverified: page budget). The Kingdom page says Trieste and Trentino-Alto Adige 'did not join the Kingdom of Italy until 1918' or 1919.

313,696 km2, 1919 only: Italy with the Trentino-Alto Adige cells (33 of 54), Trieste, 75 Albanian cells, Croatia 9, Slovenia 7, Montenegro 2 and Turkey 3. Kingdom page: 'In 1919 it annexed Trieste and Trentino-Alto Adige/Sudtirol'. The Albanian, Montenegrin and Anatolian cells are armistice-period holdings that no page opened dates (Albania 25 cells in 1917, 75 here).

299,478 km2, 1920-1931: Trentino-Alto Adige now 51 of 54 cells, Istria, Zara. Rapallo page: signed 12 November 1920, giving Italy 'Istria and the territory to the north', Trieste, Pula, Gorizia, Zadar and the islands of Cres, Losinj, Lastovo and Palagruza. The shape keeps 11 Turkish cells (Antalya region) to 1931; the pages opened are silent on any Italian zone in Anatolia (unverified: page budget; a gap-filler should date its end).
295,590 km2, 1932-1935: the 1920 outline without Turkey. Fiume was annexed under the 1924 Treaty of Rome (Rapallo page); the Dodecanese were Italian under Lausanne (1923).
295,325 km2, 1936-1937. Infobox area 310,190 km2 for 1936: ratio 0.95, fine.
295,301 km2, 1938 only: unchanged from 1936.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but Albania is a protectorate drawn as a vassal tint (status change only)

Italian Empire page: 'In 1939, Italy invaded and captured Albania', which became 'a separate kingdom in personal union with the Italian crown'; the Kingdom page: 'an Italian protectorate since 1939'. Albania is a protectorate (vassal tint), not Italian territory.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but the French cells are an occupation (hatched) and Albania a protectorate (status change only)

keyframe_review.note: 326,075 km2, 1940 only: adds 12 French cells. Kingdom page: Italy 'entered World War II ... in 1940' and lists 'southern France with Monaco' among occupied territories (undated). The French cells are an occupation (hatched), Albania a protectorate.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but Montenegro, the Greek zone and the French zone are occupations (hatched), Albania a protectorate, and only Dalmatia, Ljubljana Province, Kotor and Kosovo are annexed (status change only)

Axis page: invasion 6 April 1941, Italian forces in Ljubljana on 12 April, Italy annexed the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia, Kosovo and the Bay of Kotor (undated); Italian Empire page: governorate of Montenegro (1941-1943), Hellenic State (1941-1943). The annexed lands are Italian; Montenegro, the Greek zone and the French zone are occupations; Albania is a protectorate.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, with the occupation and protectorate statuses of 1941 (status change only)

keyframe_review.note: 427,873 km2, 1942 only: the Greek zone grows to 206 cells. Italian Empire page: Hellenic State (1941-1943); the page does not date the extension. Status as in 1941.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but for January to 8 September 1943; the occupations and the protectorate of Albania end with the armistice (years change only)

keyframe_review.note: 455,534 km2, 1943 only, the row's maximum: adds Corsica and south-eastern France (105 French cells). Italian Empire page: 'November 1942: Italian-occupied France was expanded with the occupation of Corsica'; 'On 8 September, the armistice was made public' (1943). The shape holds for January-August 1943 only.

correction.text: the 1945 shape as a stand-in for 1944: the kingdom's holdings were the part of Italy not held by the German-backed Italian Social Republic, whose front the pages do not give

keyframe_review.note: 267 km2, 1944 only: only the Tientsin concession (China, 1 cell); the Italian Empire page says the concession was ceded to Japan's puppet regime 'later in 1943'. The kingdom of 1944 is the Italy south of the German front, with Brindisi as de facto capital (Kingdom page infobox, 1943-1944); no page opened maps the front, so the 1945 outline stands in for it (unverified: page budget).
289,198 km2, 1945 only: Italy within its pre-1947 borders (Slovenia 2 cells, Austria 4). Infobox 310,190 km2 (1936): ratio 0.93.

correction.text: the 1945 shape for 1946, the year of the referendum

keyframe_review.note: 340 km2, 1946 only: again the Tientsin cell. The kingdom's last months: referendum on 2 June 1946, Umberto II's reign ends 13 June, monarchy abolished 18 June 1946 (Kingdom page).

ledger.note: 17 March 1861: the Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed. The Sardinian government declared 'a united Italian kingdom' and Victor Emmanuel II was 'proclaimed King of Italy' (infobox 'Proclamation: 17 March 1861'). The page names no boundary; the 1862 shape stands for the first year.
1865: the capital moves from Turin to Florence (infobox: Turin 1861-1865, Florence 1865-1871).

region.text: Venetia, Friuli and the Trentino front

ledger.note: June 1866: war with Austria for Veneto. 'Three days later, Italy declared war on Austria and started military operations on 23 June' (infobox 20 June); the Italian advance reached Udine on 22 July and Garibaldi won at Bezzecca on 21 July.

region.text: Venetia, Friuli and the Trentino front

ledger.note: 12 August 1866: the Armistice of Cormons. 'The cessation of hostilities between Italy and Austria was agreed to at the Armistice of Cormons signed on 12 August'; Garibaldi was ordered to evacuate Trentino on 9 August ('Obbedisco').

region.text: modern Veneto, parts of Friuli and the city of Mantua

ledger.note: October 1866: Venice joins Italy. The Treaty of Vienna of 3 October 1866 confirmed the cession of 'modern Veneto, parts of Friuli and the city of Mantua'; Napoleon III 'ceded Venetia to Italy on 19 October'; 99.9% voted for union in the plebiscite of 21-22 October.

region.text: Rome and the remaining Papal territory (Lazio)

ledger.note: 20 September 1870: Italian troops enter Rome. 'Italian troops entered Rome in 1870, ending more than one thousand years of Papal temporal power' (infobox: Capture of Rome 20 September 1870). The page names Rome, not Lazio; the region is the researcher's reading.
1871: Rome becomes the capital (infobox: Rome 1871-1946).

1882: the government takes over Assab. A navigation company bought Assab Bay in 1869; 'This was taken over by the Italian government in 1882, becoming modern Italy's first overseas territory.' Cliopatria draws the Eritrean cells from 1885.

February 1885: Italy annexes Massawa. 'By secret agreement with Britain, it annexed the port of Massawa in Eritrea'; the Kingdom page: Italy 'landed soldiers at Massawa' in 1885. The former holder is not named on the pages; Cliopatria's Khedivate of Egypt row ends in 1884.

1889: the Treaty of Wuchale. Italy 'signed the Treaty of Wuchale in 1889 with Menelik II', which 'ceded Ethiopian territory around Massawa to Italy to form the colony of Italian Eritrea'. The Kingdom page has 'In 1888, Italy annexed Massawa by force, creating the colony of Italian Eritrea'.

1890: Eritrea becomes a colony in its own right. Cliopatria's Italian Africa row begins in 1890; the Italian Africa dossier draws the colony as a tint of this state. The page gives no 1890 date (infobox 1882; Wuchale 1889).
7 September 1901: Italy gets a concession at Tientsin. 'On 7 September 1901, a concession in Tientsin was ceded to Italy by the Qing Dynasty'; possession was taken 'on 7 June 1902'.

1912: Italy holds the Dodecanese. Cliopatria's shape adds the islands in 1912; the page is silent on May 1912 and the Treaty of Ouchy and says only that the 1923 Lausanne treaty 'formalized Italian administration' of them. Italy declared war on the Ottoman Empire in October 1911 and gained Libya, which the Italian Africa dossier draws.
June 1917: the Albanian protectorate. 'In June 1917, general Giacinto Ferrero proclaimed the Italian-controlled territory in Albania to be independent under Italian protection.'

region.text: the cells of the 1917 shape that the 1918 shape lacks (Friuli, eastern Veneto)

ledger.note: October-November 1917: Caporetto. The battle 'took place from 24 October to 19 November 1917' and the Central Powers advanced '150 kilometres (93 mi) to the Piave River' (Caporetto page); Friuli and eastern Veneto are the researcher's reading of the land behind the Piave (Cliopatria's 1918 shape lacks them). The page puts the counter-offensive of Vittorio Veneto 'on the anniversary of Caporetto'. [Reviewer eu-13-b, 2026-10-25: re-dated from 1918 (confidence 1, no page) to October 1917 on the Caporetto page.]
1919: Trieste and the Trentino-Alto Adige. 'In 1919 it annexed Trieste and Trentino-Alto Adige/Sudtirol.' The page does not name the ceding state; Austria-Hungary ended in 1918.

region.text: the Italian cells that the 1919 shape adds to the 1918 shape

ledger.note: 1919: Friuli and Veneto restored. The cells the 1918 shape lacks are back in 1919; the page does not date their recovery.

region.text: the Italian-held part of Albania with the Bay of Vlore

ledger.note: 1920: Italy leaves Albania's Bay of Vlore. 'In 1920, an Albanian rebellion led the Italians to agree to return the occupied bay of Vlore to Albania.'

region.text: Istria, Zadar and the islands of Cres, Losinj and Lastovo

ledger.note: 12 November 1920: the Treaty of Rapallo. Italy gets 'Istria and the territory to the north of the peninsula', Trieste, Pula and Gorizia, Zadar ('as the Province of Zara') and the islands of Cres, Losinj, Lastovo and Palagruza; the Free State of Fiume is set up.
1923: the Dodecanese are formally Italian. The Treaty of Lausanne 'formalized Italian administration of both Libya and the Dodecanese Islands'.
1923: Lausanne confirms Italy in the Dodecanese. The treaty is with the new Turkish state, the Ottoman Empire's successor.
1924: Fiume. The Free State of Fiume was annexed by Italy 'under the 1924 Treaty of Rome'.

region.text: the Turkish cells of the 1920-1931 shape

ledger.note: 1932: the Turkish cells leave the shape. Cliopatria keeps 11 cells in Turkey (Antalya region) from 1919 to 1931; no page opened gives an Italian zone in Anatolia or its end (confidence 1; the loss is probably much earlier).

1939: Albania is invaded and made a protectorate. 'In 1939, Italy invaded and captured Albania', made 'a part of the Italian Empire as a separate kingdom in personal union with the Italian crown'; the Kingdom page: 'an Italian protectorate since 1939'.

region.text: the Italian-occupied zone in the south of France

ledger.note: 1940: the first French cells. Italy 'entered World War II ... in 1940' and the page lists 'southern France with Monaco' among occupied territories without a date; Cliopatria's 1940 shape adds 12 French cells.

region.text: Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia, the Bay of Kotor and Kosovo: the Yugoslav-side cells that Cliopatria's 1941 shape adds

ledger.note: April-May 1941: the Yugoslav partition. Invasion on 6 April, Italian forces in Ljubljana on 12 April; Italy 'annexed the southern part as the Ljubljana Province', 'large sections of Dalmatia', Kosovo and the Bay of Kotor (all undated on the page; the Treaties of Rome of 18 May 1941 ratified the Croatian state).
1941: Montenegro under Italian rule. 'Italian governorate of Montenegro (1941-1943)'; the Axis page: Italy 'gained control over Montenegro'.

region.text: the Italian zone in occupied Greece, 1941

ledger.note: 1941: the Italian zone in Greece. 'The Italians gained control over portions of both occupied Yugoslavia and occupied Greece'; 'Hellenic State (Greece) (1941-1943)'.

region.text: the Italian zone in occupied Greece, extended in 1942

ledger.note: 1942: the Italian zone in Greece widens (Greece 30 to 206 cells in Cliopatria's shape); the page does not date the extension.

region.text: Corsica and the extension of Italian-occupied France

ledger.note: November 1942: Italy occupies Corsica. 'Italian-occupied France was expanded with the occupation of Corsica' as the Germans occupied Vichy France; Cliopatria draws south-eastern France as well from 1943.
1943: the Tientsin concession goes. 'Later in 1943 the Italian Social Republic formally ceded control of the concession to Japan's puppet regime.'
1943: the seat of government moves to Brindisi (infobox: Brindisi 1943-1944, de facto).

September 1943: Italy leaves Albania. Italian troops 'were withdrawn starting in September 1943 after the fall of Mussolini'; the Axis page: 'the former Italian kingdoms of Albania and of Montenegro were placed under German occupation'.

region.text: the Italian-occupied zone in the south of France

ledger.note: 8 September 1943: the armistice. 'On 8 September, the armistice was made public'; the occupations of France, Greece and Montenegro end with it.

region.text: Corsica and the extension of Italian-occupied France

ledger.note: September 1943: Corsica and south-eastern France leave Italian hands with the armistice.

September 1943: the Governorate of Montenegro falls with the armistice. The Axis page: 'On 8 September 1943, the Italians concluded an armistice with the Allies, leaving 17 divisions stranded in Yugoslavia.'

region.text: the Italian zone in occupied Greece, 1941

ledger.note: September 1943: the Italian zone in Greece ends with the armistice (Hellenic State dated 1941-1943).

region.text: the Italian zone in occupied Greece, extended in 1942

ledger.note: September 1943: the widened Italian zone in Greece ends with the armistice.

region.text: Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia, the Bay of Kotor and Kosovo: the Yugoslav-side cells that Cliopatria's 1941 shape adds

ledger.note: September 1943: Dalmatia and the Ljubljana Province are lost. 'The Italian Governorship of Dalmatia was disestablished' after the armistice; the page does not say who took the land, nor when (confidence 1).

September 1943: the north falls to the Germans. After the surrender 'German forces established the Italian Social Republic' in occupied northern and central Italy; the kingdom keeps the south, with Brindisi as de facto capital (1943-1944). The page gives no front line, so the region is the researcher's reading.
1945: the north returns. Cliopatria's 1945 shape is the whole country; the page gives no liberation date or front line.
1945: Rome is the capital again (infobox: Rome 1871-1946, Brindisi only 1943-1944).

June 1946: the monarchy ends. The 'institutional referendum on 2 June' 'established a republic and abolished the monarchy'; Umberto II's reign ends 13 June and the monarchy is abolished on 18 June 1946.

wars.name: Third Italian War of Independence

zones.text: modern Veneto, parts of Friuli and the city of Mantua

wars.outcome: Armistice of Cormons 12 August; Treaty of Vienna 3 October 1866; Venetia ceded through Napoleon III on 19 October and annexed after the plebiscite of 21-22 October. Trentino and Trieste stayed Austrian until 'the end of World War I'.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War

zones.text: Libya, drawn by the Italian Africa and Libya dossiers

wars.outcome: War declared on the Ottoman Empire in October 1911; Italy gained Libya; the Dodecanese were Italian-administered, formalised by the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne.
wars.note: The Italian Empire page is silent on the months of 1912 and on the Treaty of Ouchy.

wars.name: Italian front of the First World War
wars.outcome: The 1915 London Pact promised Italy the lands it annexed in 1919: Trieste and Trentino-Alto Adige; Zara and the Dalmatian islands came with Rapallo in 1920.
wars.note: No war page was opened; the years 1915-1918 come from the London Pact (1915) and the page's 1918 mention.

wars.name: Albanian rebellion against the Italian protectorate
wars.outcome: An Albanian rebellion 'led the Italians to agree to return the occupied bay of Vlore to Albania' in 1920.
wars.note: Wikipedia's article is the Vlora War; it was not opened.

wars.name: Italian invasion of Albania
wars.outcome: 'In 1939, Italy invaded and captured Albania', which became a separate kingdom in personal union with the Italian crown.

wars.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia and Italian annexations

zones.text: Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia, the Bay of Kotor and Kosovo: the Yugoslav-side cells that Cliopatria's 1941 shape adds

wars.outcome: Invasion on 6 April 1941; Italian forces entered Ljubljana on 12 April; Yugoslavia surrendered on 17 April; Italy annexed the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia, Kosovo and the Bay of Kotor and ruled Montenegro as a governorate.

wars.name: Italian occupation of Greece

zones.text: the Italian zone in occupied Greece, extended in 1942

wars.outcome: 'Hellenic State (Greece) (1941-1943)': the Italians controlled portions of occupied Greece until the armistice of 8 September 1943.
wars.note: No war page was opened; the Greek campaign of 1940-1941 is not dated on the pages.

wars.name: Italian occupation of Corsica and south-eastern France

zones.text: Corsica and the extension of Italian-occupied France

wars.outcome: 'Italian-occupied France was expanded with the occupation of Corsica' in November 1942; the occupation ends with the armistice of September 1943.

wars.name: German occupation of northern and central Italy
wars.outcome: After the September 1943 surrender 'German forces established the Italian Social Republic' in the occupied north and centre; the kingdom's army, the 'Italian Co-belligerent Army', fought on the other side.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the Social Republic or the front; 1945 is the Cliopatria shape year.

certainty.note: State frontiers with the Papal States (to 1870), Austria (Treaty of Vienna, 3 October 1866) and France; the Eritrean and Tientsin holdings are small and approximate.

The 1920 Treaty of Rapallo fixes the eastern frontier by article and a boundary commission; the occupation zones in Albania (1917-1920, 1939-1943), Montenegro, Greece and France, and the concessions, are approximate.
The front between the kingdom and the German-held Social Republic is not on the pages.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by the Phase B agent for batch eu-13-b. Savoyard half of the split of Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Italy' row (587..1946, 48 shapes): this dossier keeps the slug kingdom-of-italy and reviews shapes 1862-1946, the state named by the row's Wikidata id (Q172579) and Wikipedia title; the Lombard shapes (587-774) are in kingdom-of-the-lombards and the medieval shapes (887-969) in kingdom-of-italy-medieval. Neighbours that use the counterpart 'kingdom-of-italy' for 587-961 should now name those two slugs; italian-africa's use of kingdom-of-italy as the metropole is correct.
Pages: five of the nine allowed for 23 shapes (Kingdom of Italy, Italian Empire, Third Italian War of Independence, Treaty of Rapallo, Axis occupation of Yugoslavia). The Wikipedia title 'Kingdom of Italy (1861-1946)' did not load (url_not_found); 'Kingdom of Italy' is the same article.
Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) 1944 and 1946 are only the Tientsin cell (267 and 340 km2): wrong; the 1945 outline stands in. (2) 1866 gives Veneto 24 of 71 cells; the full Veneto and Friuli arrive in 1868 although the treaty is October 1866; Lazio arrives in 1871 although Rome fell on 20 September 1870. (3) Eritrea is drawn twice in 1890-1904 (here and in Italian Africa). (4) The Tientsin concession (1901-1902) is drawn from 1905 and survives in the shapes to 1946 although it was ceded to Japan's puppet regime in 1943. (5) 11 Turkish cells (Antalya region) are kept 1919-1931 with no page. (6) Albania (1917-1920, 1939-1943), Montenegro, Greece and France are protectorate or occupation, not territory: status changes recorded in the keyframes and as vassal and occupation events.
Not settled: the First World War front (the 1918 loss of Friuli and eastern Veneto, the 1919 extra cells in Albania, Montenegro and Turkey) and the end of the Anatolian zone: no page opened covers them (confidence 1 events). Libya (1911-1912), Somalia and Ethiopia are the Italian Africa and Libya dossiers' lands; their wars are listed only where the pages date them. The Italian Social Republic and the front of 1943-1945 are not mapped: events use northern Italy and Tuscany as the researcher's reading (confidence 1-2); the 1947 Treaty of Paris (Dodecanese to Greece, border changes with Yugoslavia and France) lies after the end of the dossier and the page opened is silent on it.
Counterparts without a dossier: italian-social-republic (1943-1945), Free State of Fiume (1920-1924), the Hellenic State/Kingdom of Greece 1941-1944 (first-hellenic-republic is Cliopatria's row, ending 1940). Place names the gazetteer may lack: Menton (not used).
Page budget: see the sibling dossiers; this state used five pages (a sixth fetch of the Kingdom page, for the monarchs and 1943-1946, is the same page).
